mapping.standard_mapping_strategy: Each selected_requirements_lab_requirement_ids entry resolves through the pinned corpus bundle to one canonical 2025 document_id:clause_id; query test for the full requirement-to-section table, query trace for one bounded direct test-to-requirement-to-section record, or query section for every mapped test at one exact clause/subsection. Summary rows also publish direct lab_requirement_id -> document_id:clause_id pairs, and coverage/status family cards publish deduplicated pair totals, so the next --summary view exposes the indexed slice's canonical section keys without expanding the full plan.
mapping.first_read_strategy: Read ROADMAP-QUICKSTART.md first. It is the compact command-oriented handoff; QUERY-CARD.md, QUERY-GUIDE.md, ROADMAP.md, and IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md are deeper references and should be opened only after a bounded query identifies the exact slice. Use plan <heading-query> to locate implementation-plan sections without printing the prose.
mapping.test_query_strategy: Use ready for exactly one next planned/source handoff, work for the single active implementation slice, focus for one exact lane's bounded candidate/status card, case for one exact plan id or TEST_CASE title with source/direct pairs/owner/execution handles, an exact test_case string for one regression, trace for one exact plan/test/requirement/section/lane handle, a stable Catch2 tag for a lane, requirement/section for reverse traceability, matrix for a bounded test/API/section/lane/family reverse view, plan <heading-query> for one implementation-plan heading path, and recent --summary --compact for the newest completion ledger entries. Do not infer work from a full-suite scan.
mapping.trace_query_strategy: trace resolves exact plan id or TEST_CASE title first, then exact Lab or contract requirement id, exact canonical 2025 document_id:clause_id (or clause-only suffix), then an exact Catch2 lane tag. case is the one-case exact handoff when the plan id/title is known; it composes trace, matrix, owner, and execution handles without fuzzy fallback. Both commands never fall back to fuzzy search; use search explicitly for discovery. Each trace row pairs the selected requirement id with its canonical 2025 subsection and title, plus the C++ source location, API surfaces, and owning roadmap families; explicit mapping.lane_owners and focused_lane_tags are ranked ahead of broad family-tag overlap so the owning family is the first handle.
mapping.matrix_query_strategy: matrix resolves one exact test, requirement, canonical 2025 subsection, lane handle, or indexed roadmap family id (or the active indexed lane when omitted) and prints one bounded row per test with exact source, status, assertion, requirement-ID, and document_id:clause_id counts. Every summary row also carries direct lab_requirement_id -> document_id:clause_id pairs. Use the shared header-binding-shell lane for the five foundation binding rows; use --json for complete arrays and trace for one direct requirement row.
mapping.focused_check_strategy: Use check --lane <exact-tag> or check --family <roadmap-family-id> as the iteration-local integrity gate: roadmap structure and 2025 references remain checked globally, while test/source and completion-ledger validation is limited to the selected lane/family. Unlocated historical rows stay visible as source drift; unscoped check is the strict whole-plan reconciliation gate. Lane and family scopes are mutually exclusive.
mapping.focused_lane_strategy: Use lanes --family <roadmap-family-id> --focused --summary --compact for the small family-owned lane selector, then use focus [<exact-catch2-tag>] --summary --compact: it resolves the active lane, separates source-located executable candidates from implemented and source-drift rows, and prints owner, requirement/section counts, and copyable lane handles. The default lanes inventory retains broad cross-cutting tags for taxonomy review. Use --json for automation; use --limit 0 only for an intentional complete candidate list.
mapping.test_source_location_strategy: Derived per query from TEST_CASE declarations beneath cpp/tests; grouped semicolon-separated plan entries resolve to each matching declaration. Entries marked source-missing-needs-reconciliation are retained for requirement history and surfaced by the unlocated query until their declaration is restored or the catalog entry is superseded.
mapping.source_plan_strategy: Use unplanned --path <source-file> to list source TEST_CASE declarations with no exact Catch2 plan row; this is a bounded reconciliation queue and never infers requirements, status, or roadmap ownership.

test_status_semantics.source-missing-needs-reconciliation: Requirement and subsection history retained, but the current checkout has no matching TEST_CASE declaration; query with unlocated before restoring or superseding the entry.
test_status_semantics.failing-test-harness: The exact TEST_CASE is source-located and mapped, but a deterministic harness expectation currently stops execution; query trace or search for failure_location/failure_summary and do not treat later assertions as evidence until the harness is repaired.

next_source_state_semantics.planned: A future C++ TEST_CASE target with its file, lane, requirement, subsection, and API contract recorded; it is not executable evidence until the declaration and plan row exist.
next_source_state_semantics.unplanned-source: A source TEST_CASE declaration exists without an exact plan row; query it with unplanned and add an explicit mapped plan row before treating it as evidence.
next_source_state_semantics.exhausted: The indexed source queue for the current lane has no remaining declarations; select the next bounded family with queue/work/focus instead of rescanning the unchanged Requirements Lab.
